fields.expected: Notion describes itself as a workspace where teams and agents think together, and the part I would want to work on is the question of where agent action should stop and human judgment should take over. I built a Playwright-based job application agent in TypeScript where free-text essays and demographic fields are architecturally prevented from being auto-filled, every mutating capability sits behind fail-closed flags like SUBMIT_ENABLED, and each application moves through an explicit state machine rather than being edited ad hoc. I did that because a single wrong autonomous action in that workflow submits a real application. I expect agents inside a shared workspace raise a similar class of problem, and I would want to help measure it rather than assume it away. At Intelehealth I designed an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case standard using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes, which is the kind of work I think matters most when generation gets cheap and judgment becomes the bottleneck. I also want to be somewhere with real users, real failure modes, and enough ownership that I am responsible for whether a system actually works.
